uw_c2_strategic_prompting.question_text: Using the CRAF framework, write a complete, structured AI prompt for the underwriting scenario below. Your response must clearly demonstrate all four CRAF elements.
uw_c2_strategic_prompting.scenario_text: You are an underwriter at Northshore Windworks Inc.'s relationship bank. The company has applied for a $7.5M term loan to fund the acquisition of two wind turbine maintenance vessels. You have completed your financial analysis and have the following anonymised inputs ready: EBITDA has grown 18% year-over-year to $3.1M; net debt-to-EBITDA is 2.4x post-transaction; the company has a strong order book covering 80% of projected revenue for the next 24 months; the main risk is customer concentration, with the top two clients representing 61% of revenue. You need to draft the 'Financial Assessment' section of the credit memo for the credit committee. Write a full CRAF-structured prompt you would submit to the AI drafting tool.

scoring_rubric.key1: The prompt clearly establishes the Context element of CRAF — specifying the underwriting role, the type of document being drafted (credit memo financial assessment section), and the audience (credit committee) so the AI understands the professional setting and purpose.
scoring_rubric.key2: The prompt includes the Role element of CRAF — explicitly instructing the AI to adopt a specific persona or voice appropriate to underwriting (e.g., acting as a senior credit analyst or underwriting assistant producing formal credit committee language).
scoring_rubric.key3: The prompt supplies the Audience/Action element of CRAF — providing the specific anonymised financial inputs (EBITDA growth, leverage ratio, order book coverage, concentration risk) as structured data for the AI to work from, and specifying the exact action required (draft the Financial Assessment section).
scoring_rubric.key4: The prompt includes the Format/Constraints element of CRAF — specifying output format requirements (e.g., paragraph structure, length, tone, use of specific headings) and at least one constraint (e.g., use only the data provided, do not infer additional figures, flag assumptions).

uw_c3_critical_eval.question_text: According to the reading, why is a 'polished paragraph with a confident-sounding ratio' potentially dangerous in an AI-generated credit document?

options.A: Because polished language signals that the AI has exceeded its approved usage parameters
options.B: Because confident presentation can make an incorrect figure appear verified when it has not been checked
options.C: Because formal language in AI output typically indicates the tool has used external data sources
options.D: Because well-structured paragraphs are harder for compliance teams to audit than bullet-point formats

uw_c3_critical_eval.explanation: The reading explicitly warns that 'a polished paragraph with a confident-sounding ratio is not the same as a verified fact.' The danger is that professional-looking AI output can make errors appear credible, causing underwriters to accept incorrect figures without verification — which is precisely what the VERIFY checklist is designed to prevent.

uw_c3_critical_eval.question_text: The reading states that underwriters 'can't outsource judgment.' In the context of the VERIFY checklist, what does this mean for how AI-generated credit summaries should be treated?

options.A: AI-generated summaries should only be used for internal drafts and never submitted to credit committees
options.B: Every AI-generated text must pass a six-step VERIFY discipline before it enters a credit decision
options.C: Underwriters should rewrite all AI output from scratch to ensure the language reflects their own judgment
options.D: AI tools should be limited to formatting tasks and excluded from any analytical or narrative work

uw_c3_critical_eval.explanation: The reading's core message is that because underwriters cannot delegate their judgment to AI, every piece of AI-generated text must be run through the VERIFY checklist — a six-step discipline — before it enters a credit decision. The checklist is the mechanism through which human judgment is applied to AI output.

uw_c3_critical_eval.question_text: According to the reading's takeaway, what is the fundamental distinction the VERIFY checklist enforces that makes it essential for underwriting work?

options.A: The distinction between AI tools that are approved for use and those that are not
options.B: The distinction between a number that looks right and a number that actually is right
options.C: The distinction between a first draft and a final credit committee submission
options.D: The distinction between quantitative financial data and qualitative risk commentary

uw_c3_critical_eval.explanation: The reading's takeaway explicitly states: 'a number that looks right and a number that is right are not the same thing, and only one of them belongs in a credit decision.' This is the fundamental distinction the VERIFY checklist enforces — ensuring that apparent accuracy is replaced by confirmed accuracy before AI output drives any underwriting decision.

uw_c3_critical_eval.question_text: Apply the VERIFY checklist to the AI-generated output below. Write a full evaluation response that works through each of the six VERIFY steps and reaches a clear conclusion about whether this output is safe to include in a credit decision.
uw_c3_critical_eval.scenario_text:
You are an underwriter reviewing a credit renewal for HarborGate Foods Ltd., a food processing and distribution company. You submitted an anonymised prompt to an AI drafting tool and received the following AI-generated paragraph for the 'Leverage and Debt Service' section of the credit memo:

'HarborGate Foods has demonstrated consistent deleveraging over the review period. Net debt-to-EBITDA has improved from 3.8x to 2.9x over the past two fiscal years, supported by EBITDA growth of approximately 14%. Interest coverage stands at 4.1x, comfortably above the covenant threshold of 3.0x, providing 37% headroom. Free cash flow conversion remains strong at 82%, indicating the company retains sufficient liquidity to service its obligations without reliance on revolving credit drawdowns.'

Your source financial model shows: Net debt-to-EBITDA moved from 3.8x to 3.1x (not 2.9x); EBITDA growth was 11% (not 14%); interest coverage is 3.8x (not 4.1x); the covenant threshold is 3.0x; and free cash flow conversion is 79% (not 82%). Apply the full VERIFY checklist and write your evaluation.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response systematically identifies and flags each specific numerical discrepancy between the AI-generated output and the source financial model (net debt-to-EBITDA 2.9x vs. 3.1x; EBITDA growth 14% vs. 11%; interest coverage 4.1x vs. 3.8x; FCF conversion 82% vs. 79%), demonstrating the verification step of checking figures against source data.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response evaluates the materiality and risk implications of the errors — specifically noting that the overstated interest coverage ratio (4.1x vs. actual 3.8x) and the understated leverage ratio affect the accuracy of the covenant headroom calculation and could mislead the credit committee about the company's true risk position.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response applies at least two additional VERIFY steps beyond numerical checking — for example: assessing whether the AI's narrative logic is internally consistent, checking whether the conclusions drawn (e.g., 'comfortable headroom') are still valid given the corrected figures, or identifying any claims in the AI output that cannot be traced to the source data provided.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response reaches a clear, justified conclusion about the AI output — stating that it cannot be used as drafted, specifying which figures must be corrected before the section enters the credit memo, and confirming that the corrected version must be re-reviewed before submission to the credit committee.

uw_c4_relationship_intel.question_text: According to the reading, what types of messages does the RELATE framework specifically help underwriters handle?

uw_c4_relationship_intel.question_text: The reading warns that a poorly worded underwriter response can have consequences beyond just damaging a relationship. What specific escalation risks does the reading identify?

uw_c4_relationship_intel.question_text: According to the reading's takeaway, what is the critical constraint the RELATE framework places on AI-generated customer communications regarding internal underwriting logic?

options.A: Internal risk ratings must always be disclosed to customers to maintain transparency
options.B: AI-generated responses must be reviewed by the relationship manager before being sent

uw_c4_relationship_intel.question_text: Using the RELATE framework, write a complete AI prompt AND the customer-facing communication it should produce for the scenario below. Your response must demonstrate all six RELATE constraints.
uw_c4_relationship_intel.scenario_text: You are an underwriter at a commercial bank. Seabright Equipment Brokers Ltd., a mid-market equipment brokerage, has held a $3.0M revolving credit facility with your bank for six years. Following your annual review, you have determined that the facility limit must be reduced to $2.2M due to a deterioration in the company's working capital cycle — days sales outstanding has stretched from 42 to 67 days over the past 18 months, and the company's net debt-to-EBITDA has risen to 3.6x. Internally, the account has been re-rated from BB to BB–. The relationship manager has asked you to draft the communication to the company's CFO informing them of the limit reduction. The CFO is known to be commercially assertive and has previously escalated issues to senior management. Write: (1) the RELATE-structured AI prompt you would use, and (2) the customer-facing message the AI should produce.

scoring_rubric.key1: The AI prompt explicitly embeds constraints that prevent internal underwriting logic from appearing in the customer message — specifically, the internal re-rating (BB to BB–), the exact net debt-to-EBITDA figure used in the decision, and any internal risk assessment language are excluded from the customer-facing output.
scoring_rubric.key2: The AI prompt and resulting customer message demonstrate the relationship-preserving elements of RELATE — the tone is professional and empathetic, acknowledges the long-standing relationship (six years), and frames the limit reduction in terms of the bank's support for the company's ongoing needs rather than as a punitive action.
scoring_rubric.key3: The customer-facing message clearly communicates the key facts the CFO needs (the new facility limit of $2.2M, the effective date or next steps) without being evasive, and includes a constructive forward-looking element (e.g., an invitation to discuss, a review timeline, or an offer of support) — demonstrating that RELATE produces actionable, not just diplomatic, communication.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response demonstrates awareness of the escalation risk posed by the assertive CFO — the prompt includes a constraint or the message includes language specifically designed to reduce the likelihood of a formal complaint or escalation (e.g., proactive offer of a call, acknowledgment of the impact, clear point of contact), consistent with RELATE's purpose of turning high-friction messages into relationship-preserving conversations.

uw_c5_data_decision.question_text: According to the reading, why does the SIFT Variance Lens describe the instinct to 'reach for the nearest explanation' when seeing a financial variance as dangerous?

options.A: Because the nearest explanation is usually the most complex one and requires specialist knowledge to evaluate

SIFT is designed to prevent underwriters from acting on a hypothesis before it has been confirmed with evidence — treating a possible explanation as a verified fact is the core risk the framework addresses.

uw_c5_data_decision.question_text: According to the reading's takeaway, what does SIFT require an underwriter to confirm before acting on an AI-generated variance hypothesis?

options.A: That the AI tool used to generate the hypothesis is on the bank's approved software list
options.B: That the variance has been reviewed by the relationship manager and the credit committee

This is the core discipline SIFT enforces — evidence-based confirmation of the cause before any decision is made.

uw_c5_data_decision.question_text: Apply the SIFT Variance Lens to the scenario below. Write a full response that works through each SIFT step and reaches a validated, evidence-backed underwriting position.
uw_c5_data_decision.scenario_text:
You are an underwriter conducting the annual review of AtlasForge Machinery Ltd., a mid-market industrial machinery manufacturer. You have run the company's financials through the Financial Variance Analyzer and the AI tool has flagged the following variances versus the prior year:

• Gross margin has declined 180 basis points (from 34.2% to 32.4%)
• Days payables outstanding has extended from 38 days to 59 days
• Revenue has grown 9% year-over-year

The AI tool has generated the following hypothesis: 'The margin compression is likely attributable to rising raw material input costs, consistent with sector-wide steel price inflation. The payables extension may reflect deliberate working capital optimisation by management.'

You have access to the following additional information: (a) AtlasForge's two largest competitors reported flat or improving margins in the same period; (b) the company's management accounts show a 6% increase in direct labour costs with no corresponding productivity improvement; (c) the CFO mentioned in a recent call that they have been 'stretching suppliers a bit' due to a short-term cash flow squeeze. Apply the full SIFT Variance Lens and write your underwriting assessment.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response applies the first SIFT step by treating the AI-generated variances as clues rather than conclusions — explicitly stating that the AI hypotheses (steel price inflation, deliberate working capital optimisation) are unconfirmed starting points that require evidence-based validation before they can drive an underwriting decision.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response interrogates the AI's margin compression hypothesis against the available evidence — specifically using the competitor data (flat/improving margins in the same period) and the management accounts (6% direct labour cost increase with no productivity gain) to challenge or refine the AI's 'sector-wide steel price inflation' explanation, demonstrating the SIFT discipline of testing hypotheses against source evidence.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response interrogates the AI's payables extension hypothesis against the available evidence — specifically using the CFO's comment about 'stretching suppliers due to a short-term cash flow squeeze' to reframe the payables extension as a potential liquidity signal rather than deliberate optimisation, demonstrating that SIFT requires the underwriter to confirm the 'why' before accepting the AI's framing.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response reaches a clear, evidence-backed underwriting position that goes beyond the AI's hypotheses — identifying the combination of margin compression (likely driven by labour cost inefficiency), payables extension (likely driven by cash flow pressure), and revenue growth as a pattern that warrants further investigation or specific credit conditions, and explicitly stating what additional evidence would be needed before a final decision is made.

uw_c6_augmented_comm.question_text: For the multi-surface underwriting workflow described below, write a full response that identifies the correct Copilot surface for each task, explains the confidentiality risk at each stage, and describes the verification check required at each handoff.
uw_c6_augmented_comm.scenario_text:
You are an underwriter managing the annual credit review for PrairiePulse Exporters Inc., a grain and pulse export company. Over the next two days, you need to complete the following tasks:

Task 1: Summarise the key themes from a 45-minute internal credit discussion that took place on a Teams call with the relationship manager and credit risk team. The discussion included the company's internal risk rating, covenant headroom concerns, and a preliminary decision to request additional security.

Task 2: Draft the 'Risk Assessment' section of the credit memo in a Word document, drawing on the financial model outputs stored in an Excel workbook on SharePoint.

Task 3: Prepare a brief internal update for the credit committee via a Teams message to the credit director, summarising the three key risks identified in the review.

Task 4: Draft an information request letter to PrairiePulse Exporters Inc.'s CFO, asking for updated management accounts and a debtor aging schedule.

For each task: identify the appropriate Copilot surface, explain the confidentiality risk specific to that surface and task, and describe the verification check you would perform before the output moves to the next stage.

scoring_rubric.key1: For Tasks 1 and 3 (Teams-based tasks), the response correctly identifies Copilot in Teams as the surface, explains the confidentiality risk of Teams summaries potentially capturing and surfacing internal risk ratings, preliminary decisions, or covenant concerns in a format that could be shared beyond the intended audience, and describes a verification check (e.g., reviewing the summary to confirm no internal rating language or preliminary decision language appears before the summary is saved or forwarded).
scoring_rubric.key2: For Task 2 (Word/Excel/SharePoint), the response correctly identifies Copilot in Word and/or Excel as the appropriate surface for drafting the risk assessment section, explains the confidentiality risk of SharePoint-linked content (e.g., the financial model) being referenced or surfaced in a document that may later be shared externally, and describes a verification check at the handoff (e.g., confirming that model-specific internal figures or SharePoint file references do not appear in the final Word document in a form that could be shared with the client).
scoring_rubric.key3: For Task 4 (the external customer letter), the response correctly identifies that this task requires the highest level of surface and content scrutiny — the output is external-facing — and explicitly describes the verification check required to ensure that no internal underwriting logic, risk ratings, covenant concerns, or preliminary decisions from Tasks 1–3 have leaked into the customer-facing information request letter.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response demonstrates the overarching principle from the reading by explicitly applying the surface-matching rule across all four tasks — showing that the choice of Copilot surface is driven by both the nature of the task and the confidentiality level of the content, and that each handoff between tasks requires a deliberate check that internal-only content has not migrated into outputs intended for a broader or external audience.

uw_c7_capstone.question_text: Design and document a complete end-to-end AI-assisted underwriting workflow for the case below. Your response must demonstrate how all six domains (SAFE, CRAF, VERIFY, RELATE, SIFT, and surface-matching) function as sequential human-gated checkpoints across the case.
uw_c7_capstone.scenario_text:

The company is seeking a $9.5M term loan and a $2.0M revolving credit facility to fund the expansion of its dry-dock facility and increase working capital capacity. The application file contains: three years of audited financials, a management-prepared five-year forecast, a detailed project cost breakdown for the dry-dock expansion, and a letter of support from the company's largest customer (representing 48% of revenue) confirming a five-year contract renewal.

Your workflow will involve: (1) preparing inputs for AI-assisted analysis, (2) drafting the financial assessment section of the credit memo, (3) evaluating AI-generated variance analysis on the company's working capital metrics, (4) communicating a request for additional information to the company's CFO (the company has previously pushed back on information requests), and (5) preparing a final integrated credit recommendation.

Write a complete workflow document that maps each of the five workflow stages to the appropriate AI framework(s), identifies the human verification checkpoint at each stage, and explains how you would ensure that every AI output is verified, labelled, and traceable before it contributes to the final credit decision.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response correctly applies SAFE at Stage 1 (input preparation) — demonstrating that all non-public identifiers, specific financial figures, internal ratings, and deal terms are abstracted before any AI prompt is written, and identifies this as the first human-gated checkpoint where the underwriter confirms that no confidential data will enter the AI tool in raw form.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response correctly applies CRAF at Stage 2 (drafting the financial assessment) and SIFT at Stage 3 (evaluating working capital variance analysis) — for CRAF, demonstrating that the AI prompt includes all four structured elements to produce a controlled credit memo draft; for SIFT, demonstrating that AI-generated variance hypotheses about working capital metrics are treated as clues requiring evidence-based confirmation before they influence the credit recommendation, with a human verification checkpoint at each stage.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response correctly applies VERIFY at the appropriate stage(s) — demonstrating that AI-generated financial figures, ratios, and narrative claims in the credit memo draft are checked against source documents before the output moves forward, and that the human verification checkpoint explicitly confirms that every figure in the AI output is accurate and traceable to a source before it is labelled as verified.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response correctly applies RELATE at Stage 4 (CFO communication) and the surface-matching principle across all stages — for RELATE, demonstrating that the AI prompt for the information request letter includes constraints preventing internal logic from leaking and is designed to manage the CFO's known tendency to push back; for surface-matching, identifying the appropriate Copilot surface for each stage and describing the handoff verification check that ensures internal-only content does not migrate into the external-facing CFO communication or the final credit recommendation.

mk_c1_responsible_ai.question_text: According to the SAFE Abstraction Method, what is the correct first step a marketer should take before entering campaign data into a generative AI tool?

options.A: Feed the data directly into Copilot to save time
options.B: Spot the sensitive or identifying information in the data
options.C: Examine the AI output for accuracy before sharing
options.D: Abstract all numerical figures into rounded estimates

mk_c1_responsible_ai.explanation: The SAFE method begins with 'S' — Spot — meaning the marketer must first identify any sensitive or identifying information in the data before taking any further action. This is the foundational step that makes the rest of the method possible.

mk_c1_responsible_ai.question_text: A marketer wants to use Copilot to draft a follow-up email sequence using a trade show lead list that includes real names, email addresses, and company details. According to the SAFE Abstraction Method, what should the marketer do with this list before prompting Copilot?

options.A: Paste the full list into the prompt to give Copilot maximum context
options.B: Only include the company names and remove personal emails
options.C: Abstract the real identifiers by replacing them with generic placeholders
options.D: Ask a colleague to review the list before submitting it to Copilot

mk_c1_responsible_ai.explanation: The 'A' step in SAFE stands for Abstract — replacing real names, emails, and other identifying details with generic placeholders before feeding the data into the AI tool. This protects personal information while still allowing Copilot to generate useful content.

mk_c1_responsible_ai.question_text: Which of the following types of data does the reading explicitly identify as information that must never leave an organization's secure environment when using generative AI tools?

options.A: Publicly available competitor pricing and industry benchmarks
options.B: Unreleased product details, customer contact records, and private campaign metrics
options.C: General marketing best practices and channel strategy frameworks
options.D: Approved brand guidelines and published case studies

mk_c1_responsible_ai.explanation: The reading explicitly lists unreleased product details, customer contact records, trade show lead lists, and private campaign metrics as examples of data that must never leave the organization's secure environment when using generative AI tools.

mk_c1_responsible_ai.question_text: Apply the SAFE Abstraction Method to the scenario below. Write a response that demonstrates each step of the method and explains what you would do at each stage.
mk_c1_responsible_ai.scenario_text: You are a Marketing Manager at Westport Composites Ltd. Your team has just completed a customer satisfaction survey. The results file contains customer names, email addresses, Net Promoter Scores, and verbatim comments — some of which reference confidential product quality issues that have not yet been publicly disclosed. Your director has asked you to use Copilot to draft a summary report and a customer communication based on these survey results.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response correctly identifies the Spot step — explicitly naming the sensitive elements in the scenario (customer names, email addresses, NPS scores, and confidential product quality comments) as information that must be flagged before proceeding.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response correctly describes the Abstract step — explaining how real customer names, emails, and identifying details would be replaced with generic placeholders (e.g., 'Customer A', 'respondent') and how confidential product issues would be removed or generalized before prompting Copilot.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response correctly describes the Feed step — demonstrating how the abstracted, de-identified data would be entered into Copilot to generate the summary report and customer communication draft.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response correctly describes the Examine step — explaining that the AI output must be reviewed to ensure no real identifiers or confidential details have re-appeared, and that the content is accurate and appropriate before it is shared with any audience.

mk_c2_strategic_prompting.question_text: According to the CRAF framework, what does the 'R' component require a marketer to specify in a prompt to Copilot?

options.A: The required word count and formatting rules for the output
options.B: The role or persona Copilot should adopt when generating the content
options.C: The research sources Copilot should reference for accuracy
options.D: The review process the content will go through after generation

mk_c2_strategic_prompting.explanation: In the CRAF framework, 'R' stands for Role — the marketer instructs Copilot to adopt a specific persona or professional role (e.g., 'act as a B2B content strategist') so the tone and expertise of the output match the intended purpose.

mk_c2_strategic_prompting.question_text: A marketer writes the following prompt: 'Write something about our new product launch.' According to the CRAF framework, what is the PRIMARY problem with this prompt?

options.A: It does not specify a word count or character limit
options.B: It is missing Context, Role, Action, and Format — all four CRAF components
options.C: It uses informal language that Copilot cannot interpret
options.D: It should be submitted in bullet-point form rather than as a sentence

mk_c2_strategic_prompting.explanation: The CRAF framework requires all four components — Context, Role, Action, and Format — to be present for Copilot to produce targeted, on-brand, channel-ready copy. The example prompt provides none of these elements, leaving Copilot without the information it needs to generate a usable output.

mk_c2_strategic_prompting.question_text: According to the reading, what is the intended outcome of using the CRAF framework when prompting Copilot for marketing content?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any human editing or review of AI-generated content
options.B: To produce targeted, on-brand, channel-ready copy that the marketer polishes rather than rebuilds
options.C: To ensure Copilot searches the internet for the most current marketing trends
options.D: To reduce the number of prompts needed by automating the briefing process

mk_c2_strategic_prompting.explanation: The reading's takeaway explicitly states that CRAF is designed to deliver 'targeted, on-brand, channel-ready copy that you polish — not rebuild,' meaning the framework aims to get a usable first draft that requires refinement rather than a complete redo.

mk_c2_strategic_prompting.question_text: Using the CRAF framework, write a complete, well-structured prompt for the scenario below. Then briefly explain how each of the four CRAF components is represented in your prompt.
mk_c2_strategic_prompting.scenario_text: You are a Marketing Communications Manager at BrightWave Electronics Inc., a B2B manufacturer of smart building sensors. BrightWave is launching a new energy-monitoring sensor aimed at facilities managers in the commercial real estate sector. You need Copilot to draft a LinkedIn post announcing the product launch that highlights energy savings, is professional in tone, and drives traffic to the product landing page.

scoring_rubric.key1: The prompt includes a clear Context component — setting the scene by identifying BrightWave Electronics Inc., the product (energy-monitoring sensor), and the target audience (facilities managers in commercial real estate).
scoring_rubric.key2: The prompt includes a clear Role component — instructing Copilot to adopt a specific persona appropriate to the task (e.g., 'act as a B2B LinkedIn content specialist' or similar professional role).
scoring_rubric.key3: The prompt includes a clear Action component — specifying what Copilot must do (e.g., 'write a LinkedIn post announcing the product launch that highlights energy savings and includes a call to action linking to the product landing page').
scoring_rubric.key4: The prompt includes a clear Format component — specifying the output format appropriate for LinkedIn (e.g., character or word count, use of emojis or hashtags, paragraph structure) and the learner's explanation correctly maps all four CRAF elements to their prompt.

mk_c3_critical_eval.question_text: According to the reading, why is speed without scrutiny described as a 'liability' for Marketing & Communications professionals using AI tools?

options.A: Because AI tools are too slow to meet real marketing deadlines without human acceleration
options.B: Because inaccurate statistics, invented quotes, or confidential details in public content can damage credibility and cause harm
options.C: Because AI-generated content always requires complete rewriting before it can be used
options.D: Because Copilot cannot process marketing briefs longer than ten pages

mk_c3_critical_eval.explanation: The reading explicitly states that 'a single inaccurate statistic, an invented quote, or a confidential detail slipping into a public post can damage credibility,' which is why speed without scrutiny is a liability — the risk is reputational and organizational harm from unreviewed AI output.

mk_c3_critical_eval.question_text: The VERIFY Checklist is designed to be applied at what point in the content creation process, according to the reading?

options.A: Before writing the prompt, to ensure the brief is complete
options.B: During the AI generation process, to guide Copilot's output in real time
options.C: After AI generates a recap or draft, before any word reaches the audience
options.D: Only when the content contains statistical data or financial figures

mk_c3_critical_eval.explanation: The reading's takeaway states that every AI-generated recap or draft must be run through the VERIFY Checklist 'before a single word reaches your audience,' making it a post-generation, pre-publication review step.

mk_c3_critical_eval.question_text: According to the reading, which of the following is explicitly listed as one of the elements the VERIFY Checklist requires marketers to check in AI-generated content?

options.A: SEO keyword density and meta description accuracy
options.B: Facts, tone, accuracy, missing elements, and confidential details
options.C: Word count compliance and brand font usage
options.D: Social media platform algorithm compatibility

mk_c3_critical_eval.explanation: The reading explicitly states that the VERIFY Checklist covers 'facts, tone, accuracy, missing elements, and confidential details' — these are the five dimensions a marketer must review in every AI-generated draft before publication.

mk_c3_critical_eval.question_text: Apply the VERIFY Checklist to the AI-generated content described in the scenario below. Write a structured evaluation that addresses each element of the checklist and identifies any issues that must be resolved before the content is published.
mk_c3_critical_eval.scenario_text: You are a Communications Manager at Lakeview Foods Inc. Copilot has generated a press release announcing a new line of plant-based snacks. The draft includes a statistic claiming '78% of consumers prefer plant-based snacks over traditional options' — you cannot find the original source for this figure. The draft also quotes your CEO saying 'This is the most significant product launch in our company's 30-year history' — but you have no record of the CEO making this statement. Additionally, the draft mentions that Lakeview Foods is currently in merger discussions with a regional distributor, which is confidential and has not been publicly disclosed. The tone throughout is enthusiastic but borders on hyperbolic.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response identifies the facts issue — flagging the unsourced '78%' statistic as unverified and explaining that it must be traced to a credible, citable source or removed from the draft before publication.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response identifies the accuracy issue — flagging the unverified CEO quote as a potential invented or hallucinated attribution and explaining that it must be confirmed directly with the CEO or removed.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response identifies the confidential details issue — flagging the mention of merger discussions as confidential, non-public information that must be removed entirely from the press release before it is distributed.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response identifies the tone issue — noting that the hyperbolic language poses a credibility risk and recommending specific revisions to bring the tone in line with professional, factual communications standards, demonstrating application of the full VERIFY Checklist.

mk_c4_relationship_intel.question_text: According to the reading, what is the core challenge the TAILOR Approach is designed to solve for account-based marketers?

options.A: Reducing the time it takes to design visual assets for personalized campaigns
options.B: Achieving personalized outreach at scale without leaking confidential information into AI tools
options.C: Automating the full outreach process so marketers can focus on strategy
options.D: Ensuring AI-generated emails comply with data privacy regulations in each market

mk_c4_relationship_intel.explanation: The reading explicitly states that the challenge TAILOR addresses is 'doing this at scale without leaking confidential information into AI tools' — the framework balances the need for personalization with the requirement to keep sensitive data out of AI systems.

mk_c4_relationship_intel.question_text: According to the TAILOR Approach, what type of information should be used when prompting AI to research and draft personalized outreach content?

options.A: Internal CRM notes and private account history to maximize personalization
options.B: Only publicly available information, with human relationship context added afterward
options.C: A combination of public and confidential data, clearly labeled in the prompt
options.D: Anonymized versions of all account data, including internal deal stages

mk_c4_relationship_intel.explanation: The reading's takeaway explicitly states: 'Use AI to research and draft with public information only, then layer in your human knowledge and relationship context afterward.' This sequencing is the defining principle of the TAILOR Approach.

mk_c4_relationship_intel.question_text: According to the reading, why is generic outreach described as 'noise' in account-based marketing?

options.A: Because it is too expensive to produce at scale compared to personalized content
options.B: Because AI tools cannot generate generic content as effectively as personalized content
options.C: Because personalized outreach grounded in real insight about a prospect's world is what earns attention
options.D: Because generic outreach violates most B2B email marketing compliance standards

mk_c4_relationship_intel.explanation: The reading contrasts generic outreach (described as 'noise') with 'personalized outreach — grounded in real insight about a prospect's world — which is what earns attention,' establishing that relevance and insight are what differentiate effective ABM outreach.

mk_c4_relationship_intel.question_text: Apply the TAILOR Approach to the scenario below. Write a response that demonstrates how you would use AI to build personalized outreach for this account while keeping confidential information protected.
mk_c4_relationship_intel.scenario_text: You are an Account-Based Marketing Manager at Montane Aerospace Corp. You are preparing a personalized outreach campaign targeting a key prospect: a large regional airline that has recently announced a fleet modernization program (this was covered in aviation trade press). Your internal CRM shows that Montane had an unsuccessful sales conversation with this airline 18 months ago due to pricing concerns, and your sales director has a personal relationship with the airline's VP of Procurement. You need to use Copilot to research the prospect and draft an initial outreach email.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response correctly identifies what information is safe to feed into Copilot — specifically the publicly available fleet modernization announcement from trade press — and explains why this public information can be used in AI prompts without risk.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response correctly identifies what information must NOT be entered into Copilot — the internal CRM notes about the failed sales conversation, pricing concerns, and the sales director's personal relationship — and explains that this confidential relationship context must be kept out of AI tools.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response demonstrates how Copilot would be prompted using only public information to research the prospect and generate a draft outreach email (e.g., referencing the fleet modernization program and Montane's relevant capabilities).
scoring_rubric.key4: The response explains how the human relationship context (prior conversation history, pricing sensitivity, personal connection to the VP of Procurement) would be layered into the final email by the marketer after Copilot produces the draft — demonstrating the TAILOR principle of AI-first drafting followed by human personalization.

mk_c5_data_decision.question_text: According to the reading, what problem does the DECIDE Framework solve for marketers using AI tools like Copilot in Excel and Power BI?

options.A: It automates the creation of campaign dashboards so marketers can focus on creative work
options.B: It ensures AI-generated marketing insights are defined, verified, and contextualised before driving budget or strategy decisions
options.C: It replaces the need for a data analyst by allowing marketers to interpret raw data independently
options.D: It standardizes the visual format of marketing reports across all business units

mk_c5_data_decision.explanation: The reading's takeaway explicitly states that the DECIDE Framework ensures 'every AI-generated marketing insight is defined, verified, and contextualised before it drives a budget or strategy decision' — addressing the risk of speed without structure leading to bad decisions.

mk_c5_data_decision.question_text: According to the reading, what recurring pressure does the DECIDE Framework help marketers address each quarter?

options.A: Producing enough creative content variations to satisfy A/B testing requirements
options.B: Turning a spreadsheet full of campaign metrics into a clear story and a smarter plan
options.C: Reducing the cost per lead across all digital marketing channels simultaneously
options.D: Aligning marketing KPIs with finance department reporting cycles

mk_c5_data_decision.explanation: The reading explicitly describes the quarterly pressure as needing to 'turn a spreadsheet full of campaign metrics into a clear story and a smarter plan' — this is the specific challenge the DECIDE Framework is designed to address.

mk_c5_data_decision.question_text: According to the reading, what is the risk of using AI tools like Copilot in Excel and Power BI without a structured framework like DECIDE?

options.A: The AI will generate visualizations that are incompatible with standard presentation software
options.B: Speed without structure leads to bad decisions
options.C: The AI will surface only historical trends and miss forward-looking projections
options.D: Marketers will over-rely on AI and lose their analytical skills over time

mk_c5_data_decision.explanation: The reading explicitly warns that 'speed without structure leads to bad decisions' when using AI tools to analyze campaign metrics — this is the core risk the DECIDE Framework is designed to mitigate.

mk_c5_data_decision.question_text: Apply the DECIDE Framework to the scenario below. Write a structured response that demonstrates how you would use the framework to move from raw AI-generated data insights to a sound marketing decision.
mk_c5_data_decision.scenario_text: You are a Marketing Manager at Atlas Marine Equipment Co. At the end of Q3, you ask Copilot in Excel to analyze your campaign performance data. Copilot surfaces the following insight: 'Email campaigns targeting port operations managers generated a 42% higher click-through rate than campaigns targeting procurement managers this quarter.' Your director wants to reallocate 30% of the Q4 digital budget away from procurement-focused campaigns and toward port operations audiences based on this finding alone. You need to apply the DECIDE Framework before recommending whether to proceed with this budget shift.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response demonstrates the Define step — clearly articulating the specific decision to be made (whether to reallocate 30% of Q4 digital budget to port operations audiences) and the question the data must answer to support that decision.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response demonstrates the verify step — questioning whether the AI-generated 42% CTR difference is statistically meaningful, checking the sample size, time period, and whether the data is complete and accurate before treating it as a reliable signal.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response demonstrates the contextualise step — considering factors beyond the raw metric that could explain the difference (e.g., seasonal buying cycles, campaign creative differences, list quality) and whether those factors affect the validity of the insight for Q4 planning.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response arrives at a structured recommendation — either supporting, modifying, or rejecting the proposed budget reallocation — with clear reasoning that shows the decision is grounded in the verified and contextualised insight rather than the raw AI output alone, demonstrating the full DECIDE process.

mk_c6_augmented_comm.question_text: According to the reading, what is the key principle a marketer should apply before writing any prompt when using M365 Copilot across multiple tools?

options.A: Always start in Microsoft Word before moving to any other M365 application
options.B: Pause and ask which M365 Copilot surface is optimised for the specific step being performed
options.C: Use the same prompt across all M365 tools to ensure consistency of output
options.D: Prioritize speed by selecting whichever tool is already open on your desktop

mk_c6_augmented_comm.explanation: The reading's takeaway explicitly states: 'Before you prompt, pause and ask which M365 Copilot surface is optimised for this specific step — research, drafting, translation, or distribution.' Matching the tool to the task is the central principle of the course.

mk_c6_augmented_comm.question_text: According to the reading, which of the following best illustrates the complexity of a single marketing deliverable that requires multiple M365 Copilot surfaces?

options.A: A social media calendar built entirely within Microsoft Excel
options.B: A bilingual client email about a market disruption requiring intelligence gathering, drafting, translation, and formatting for distribution
options.C: A product brochure designed in PowerPoint using Copilot's image generation feature
options.D: A weekly internal newsletter drafted in Microsoft Word and distributed via SharePoint

mk_c6_augmented_comm.explanation: The reading uses the specific example of 'a bilingual client email about a market disruption' that requires gathering intelligence, drafting copy, translating it, and formatting it for distribution — explicitly illustrating how a single deliverable can span multiple M365 Copilot surfaces.

mk_c6_augmented_comm.question_text: According to the reading, what is the result of matching the right M365 Copilot tool to the right task in a communications workflow?

options.A: It eliminates the need for human review before the communication is sent
options.B: It turns a generic AI output into a polished, bilingual communication ready to send
options.C: It allows the marketer to complete the entire workflow within a single M365 application
options.D: It ensures the communication automatically complies with regional language regulations

mk_c6_augmented_comm.explanation: The reading's takeaway states that matching the tool to the task 'is what turns a generic AI output into a polished, bilingual communication ready to send' — the quality improvement comes specifically from deliberate tool selection at each workflow stage.

mk_c6_augmented_comm.question_text: Apply the M365 Copilot multi-surface workflow principle to the scenario below. Write a response that maps each stage of the communication task to the most appropriate M365 Copilot surface and explains why each tool is the right choice for that step.
mk_c6_augmented_comm.scenario_text: You are a Marketing Communications Manager at NovaTech Innovations Inc., a technology solutions provider. A major supply chain disruption has affected one of NovaTech's key product lines, and you need to communicate proactively with your top 50 enterprise clients in both English and French. The communication must: (1) summarize the disruption and its likely impact on delivery timelines, (2) reassure clients with a clear mitigation plan, (3) be translated accurately into French, and (4) be distributed to the correct client contacts via email. You are working under a tight two-hour deadline.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response identifies an appropriate M365 Copilot surface for the intelligence-gathering or research step (e.g., Copilot in Teams or Copilot in Bing/Edge to gather information about the disruption and its scope) and explains why this tool is suited to that task.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response identifies an appropriate M365 Copilot surface for the drafting step (e.g., Copilot in Word or Outlook to draft the client communication covering the disruption summary and mitigation plan) and explains why this tool is suited to drafting structured, professional communications.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response identifies an appropriate M365 Copilot surface or feature for the translation step (e.g., Copilot in Word with translation capability, or a designated translation tool within M365) and explains why accurate translation requires a deliberate tool choice rather than a generic prompt.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response identifies an appropriate M365 Copilot surface for the distribution step (e.g., Copilot in Outlook to personalize and send the email to the correct client contacts from the list) and explains how matching the distribution tool to this final step ensures the communication reaches the right audience efficiently — demonstrating the full multi-surface workflow principle.

mk_c7_capstone.question_text: According to the reading, what distinguishes an End-to-End AI Workflow from simply using AI for isolated tasks?

options.A: An End-to-End AI Workflow uses only one AI tool throughout the entire project to ensure consistency
options.B: An End-to-End AI Workflow deliberately integrates AI assistance at every stage of a marketing project as a connected chain
options.C: An End-to-End AI Workflow automates all stages of a project without requiring human input at any point
options.D: An End-to-End AI Workflow is only applicable to large-scale campaigns with dedicated data science support

mk_c7_capstone.explanation: The reading explicitly defines an End-to-End AI Workflow as 'deliberately integrating AI assistance at every stage of a marketing project — not just reaching for it when you're stuck on a single task,' emphasizing the connected, intentional nature of the approach.

mk_c7_capstone.question_text: According to the reading, what does an End-to-End AI Workflow look like for Marketing & Communications professionals in terms of the stages where AI provides assistance?

options.A: AI assists only with content creation and social media scheduling
options.B: AI assists with profiling and prioritizing prospects during planning, through execution, evaluation, and reporting
options.C: AI assists primarily with post-campaign analysis and budget forecasting
options.D: AI assists with compliance checking and legal review of all marketing materials

mk_c7_capstone.explanation: The reading describes the End-to-End AI Workflow as 'a connected chain: AI helps you profile and prioritize prospects during planning' and continues through execution, evaluation, and reporting — covering all stages of a marketing project.

mk_c7_capstone.question_text: According to the reading, what safeguard must be maintained at every stage of an End-to-End AI Workflow, regardless of how much AI assistance is used?

options.A: A secondary AI tool must verify all outputs from the primary AI tool before they are used
options.B: All AI-generated content must be submitted to the legal department for approval
options.C: A human review gate must be maintained at every output before data, content, or insights move forward
options.D: The workflow must be documented and approved by senior leadership before execution begins

mk_c7_capstone.explanation: The reading's takeaway explicitly states: 'keep a human review gate at every output before data, content, or insights move forward' — this is the non-negotiable safeguard that applies at every stage of the End-to-End AI Workflow.

mk_c7_capstone.question_text: Design an End-to-End AI Workflow for the scenario below. Your response should map AI assistance across all major stages of the project, identify which frameworks or tools from the course apply at each stage, and specify where human review gates must be placed.
mk_c7_capstone.scenario_text: You are the Head of Marketing at ExportBoost Program, a government-backed initiative that helps small and medium-sized businesses enter new export markets. ExportBoost is launching a six-week campaign to recruit 200 new SME participants for its next export readiness cohort. The campaign will include: targeted outreach to pre-qualified SME prospects, a content series (blog posts, LinkedIn posts, and an email nurture sequence), performance tracking against a weekly enrollment target, and a post-campaign report for the program's executive board. You have a small team of two and a modest budget. Design your End-to-End AI Workflow for this campaign.

scoring_rubric.key1: The response maps AI assistance to the planning and prospecting stage — describing how AI (e.g., using the TAILOR Approach) would be used to profile and prioritize SME prospects using public information, with a human review gate before any outreach list is finalized.
scoring_rubric.key2: The response maps AI assistance to the content creation and execution stage — describing how AI (e.g., using the CRAF framework) would be used to draft blog posts, LinkedIn posts, and email sequences, with a human review gate (e.g., VERIFY Checklist) applied to every piece of content before it is published or sent.
scoring_rubric.key3: The response maps AI assistance to the performance tracking and evaluation stage — describing how AI (e.g., using the DECIDE Framework in Excel or Power BI) would be used to analyze weekly enrollment data and surface insights, with a human review gate before any insights are used to adjust campaign tactics or budget.
scoring_rubric.key4: The response maps AI assistance to the reporting stage — describing how AI would be used to synthesize campaign results into a draft executive board report, and specifies a final human review gate to verify accuracy, tone, and completeness before the report is presented — demonstrating a fully connected End-to-End AI Workflow with human oversight at every stage.
